findings.title: Write lock is acquired without re-checking the cache and is held across file I/O
findings.body: After acquiring entryPointAssetsCacheMu.Lock(), GetWebAssets does not check entryPointAssetsCache again before reloading. Concurrent callers that all missed the initial RLock fast path will queue on the write lock and then each sequentially repeat readWebAssetsFromFile (and overwrite the cache) while holding the lock across disk I/O. This serializes cold-start (and every Dev-mode) requests and performs redundant manifest reads instead of letting all but the first caller reuse the newly populated cache; add a double-checked cache test inside the write lock and return the cached value when another goroutine populated it.

findings.title: No concurrent test covers the race being fixed
findings.body: The change adds synchronization around the global entryPointAssetsCache but no test exercises concurrent GetWebAssets calls, so a regression (e.g. a future unsynchronized access to the cache) would not be caught even under `go test -race`. Add a test that calls GetWebAssets from multiple goroutines in parallel (covering both the cached fast path and the initial load) and run it with the race detector.
